answer_1.quote: We introduced ChartGaze, a novel dataset that captures how humans visually process charts. By capturing high-precision human gaze patterns for chart-based questions, ChartGaze enables detailed comparisons between human and model attention. This opens up new insights into how human gaze can serve as an implicit training signal to enhance LVLM performance on chart understanding.
answer_1.outputs: Answers to chart-based yes/no questions; attention maps

answer_2.quote: Since our dataset consists of yes/no questions, we use accuracy, defined as the percentage of questions correctly answered, to compare chart understanding performance across different models. To assess the similarity between the LVLM attention maps and the human attention maps, we used three standard metrics commonly used in saliency prediction. Pearson's Correlation Coefficient (CC), Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, and histogram intersection (also known as similarity or SIM metric) between the ground-truth human gaze distribution and the model's attention distribution over the chart image.

answer_4.quote: To ensure the correctness of our generated questions, we had human annotators flag ambiguous or incorrect questions during data collection... We also verified the quality of the GPT-generated answers by measuring agreement with human annotators. A random sample of 100 examples showed a 93% agreement between GPT-4o and the majority vote of our seven human annotators. The highest pairwise agreement among human annotators was 92%.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators flagged ambiguous or incorrect questions; verified GPT-4o answers via agreement with human annotators.
